video.title: The Pros Swing Differently Than You (with lesson transformation)

classification.reason: The coach provides executable drills and cues, such as doing heavy hopper swings with a stabilized elbow and using feet to align contact with the throwing slot.

problem.title_as_question: Why are recreational players unable to drive high balls or harness body rotation on the forehand?
problem.definition: Players swing the arm underhand in a low-to-high path to create net clearance, which prevents rotational energy from passing through the shoulder throwing chain and makes driving high balls biomechanically impossible.

symptoms.description: The elbow pulls in close to the torso and chicken-wings on high balls, making it feel impossible to drive the racket through.
The swing finish ends up high over the shoulder instead of low around the back pocket or hip.
The player feels that rotating the hips or body does not help power or stabilize the swing, staying sideways instead.

causes.statement: Rotational energy is not harnessed because energy cannot pass through the shoulder into an overhand throwing chain.
The brain fears hitting into the ground and forces the arm to swing underhand and low-to-high, not understanding forearm pronation produces lift.
The elbow drops in toward the body because the back, rotator cuff, scapula, and chest fail to stabilize it up in a throwing posture.
The brain matches arm movement to the large, visible low-to-high motion of the pro's racket rather than the actual high-to-low throwing arm action.

angles.summary: Forearm supination and pronation cause the racket head to move low-to-high and square up even when the arm and elbow throw level or high-to-low.
Players copy the low-to-high arc of the racket seen on pro footage instead of copying the pro arm's overhand throwing mechanics.
The coach demonstrates an underhand swing ending high over the shoulder versus an overhand throwing swing ending down at the back pocket.

solutions.summary: Perform shadow overhand throwing swings at home while maintaining haptic racket face awareness aligned to a piece of tape on a net or wall.
solutions.external_goal: Align the throwing path and racket face to a piece of red tape on the net or wall.

solutions.summary: Perform overhand swings with a heavy ball hopper or weight to force the elbow to stay up and stabilized by the shoulder, lat, and back muscles.
solutions.external_goal: Swing a heavy ball hopper while keeping the elbow raised and stable.

solutions.summary: Have a partner toss high balls and use active footwork steps to position the body so the ball meets the pre-felt throwing contact slot.
solutions.external_goal: Use footwork to position the high ball directly into the contact hitting slot.

solutions.summary: From the baseline, deliberately aim to drill the top tape of the net with an overhand throw, trusting forearm roll to send the ball 3 feet over.
solutions.external_goal: Try to drill the top of the net tape.
